questions.title: Layers of the tear film
questions.question: About the layers of the tear film:

options.A: The innermost mucin layer is produced by Meibomian glands
options.B: The superficial lipid layer is produced by conjunctival goblet cells
options.C: The aqueous (watery) layer is the middle, thickest layer
options.D: The middle layer is produced by Meibomian glands

explanations.A: Incorrect. The innermost mucin layer is produced by conjunctival GOBLET cells, not Meibomian glands (which make the lipid layer).
explanations.B: Incorrect. The superficial lipid layer is produced by the MEIBOMIAN glands; goblet cells make the mucin layer, not the lipid layer.
explanations.C: Correct. The tear film is three-layered, and the middle aqueous (watery) layer, secreted by the lacrimal and accessory lacrimal glands, is the thickest, carrying most of the tear volume and its dissolved substances. The lipid layer is superficial and the mucin layer innermost. Hence the aqueous layer is the middle, thickest layer.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The middle (aqueous) layer is produced by the LACRIMAL glands; the Meibomian glands make the superficial lipid layer.

questions.learning_objective: Recall the three tear-film layers, their glands and the thickest layer.

questions.title: Accessory eye structures (eyelid glands)
questions.question: Concerning the accessory eye structures:

options.A: Inflammation of Zeis sebaceous glands causes chalazion formation
options.B: Moll's glands are apocrine sweat glands in the eyelid
options.C: The nasolacrimal duct is lined by simple columnar non-ciliated epithelium
options.D: The bulbar conjunctiva lines the inner surface of the eyelid

explanations.A: Incorrect. Inflammation of a Zeis (sebaceous) gland with its lash follicle produces a STYE (external hordeolum); a chalazion is a granuloma of a blocked Meibomian gland.
explanations.B: Correct. Moll's glands are modified apocrine sweat glands of the eyelid margin, opening near the eyelash follicles. This is the accurate statement among the options.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The nasolacrimal duct is lined by pseudostratified/stratified columnar epithelium, not simple columnar non-ciliated epithelium.
explanations.D: Incorrect. It is the PALPEBRAL conjunctiva that lines the inner surface of the eyelid; the bulbar conjunctiva covers the anterior sclera.

questions.learning_objective: Recall eyelid gland histology, distinguishing Moll, Zeis and Meibomian glands.

questions.title: Middle ear boundaries and contents
questions.question: As regards the middle ear boundaries and contents, select the correct answer:

options.A: The handle of the malleus fits into the oval window
options.B: The tensor tympani and stapedius muscles regulate sound conduction
options.C: The auditory tube is lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium
options.D: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear cavity to the oropharynx

explanations.A: Incorrect. The handle of the malleus is attached to the tympanic membrane; it is the STAPES footplate that sits in the oval window.
explanations.B: Correct. The tensor tympani (attached to the malleus, supplied by V3) and the stapedius (attached to the stapes, supplied by the facial nerve) are the two intratympanic muscles. Their reflex contraction stiffens the ossicular chain and dampens its vibration, so it regulates sound conduction through the middle ear. This attenuation (acoustic) reflex protects the inner ear from damagingly loud sounds.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The auditory (Eustachian) tube is lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, not stratified cuboidal epithelium.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the NASOPHARYNX, not the oropharynx.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the middle-ear muscles and correct common middle-ear anatomy errors.

questions.title: Supporting cells of the organ of Corti
questions.question: Regarding the organ of Corti, the following is correct:

options.A: Phalangeal cells make direct support to hair cells
options.B: Outer hair cells are arranged as one row
options.C: Inner phalangeal cells are arranged as 3-4 rows
options.D: The organ of Corti is a neuroreceptor for equilibrium

explanations.A: Correct. The phalangeal cells (inner phalangeal and outer/Deiters' cells) are the supporting cells that directly support the hair cells, cupping their bases and extending processes to the reticular lamina. They are the immediate structural support of the hair cells.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The OUTER hair cells are arranged in three (to four) rows; it is the INNER hair cells that form a single row.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Inner phalangeal cells accompany the single row of inner hair cells; the 3-4-row arrangement belongs to the outer hair cells/Deiters' cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The organ of Corti is the neuroreceptor for HEARING; equilibrium is detected by the vestibular maculae and cristae.

questions.learning_objective: Recall the supporting cells and hair-cell arrangement of the organ of Corti.

questions.title: Hair cells of the vestibular maculae
questions.question: Regarding the maculae of the utricle and saccule:

options.A: They lie parallel to each other
options.B: They are covered by a proteoglycan membrane called the tectorial membrane
options.C: They have type 1 and type 2 mechanoreceptor hair cells
options.D: The supporting cell has an apical true cilium (kinocilium)

explanations.A: Incorrect. The utricular and saccular maculae lie roughly PERPENDICULAR to each other (utricle horizontal, saccule vertical), not parallel, which lets them detect linear acceleration in different planes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The maculae are covered by a gelatinous OTOLITHIC (statoconial) membrane bearing otoconia; the tectorial membrane belongs to the cochlear organ of Corti.
explanations.C: Correct. The macular sensory epithelium contains type 1 (flask-shaped, with a chalice/calyx nerve ending) and type 2 (cylindrical) mechanoreceptor hair cells, the same two hair-cell types found in the cristae. This is the correct statement.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The true kinocilium is on the HAIR cell (with the stereocilia), not on the supporting cell.

questions.learning_objective: Recall the hair-cell types and otolithic membrane of the vestibular maculae.

questions.title: Ascending spinal cord tracts
questions.question: Select the correct answer regarding the ascending spinal tracts:

options.A: The ventral spinocerebellar tract originates from cells in the gracile and cuneate nuclei
options.B: The external arcuate fibres arise from Clarke's nucleus
options.C: The spinotectal tract is concerned with the spino-visual reflex
options.D: The spino-olivary tract originates from cells in laminae I and V in the posterior horn

explanations.A: Incorrect. The ventral (anterior) spinocerebellar tract arises from spinal border cells in the lower thoracic/lumbar cord, not from the gracile and cuneate nuclei (which are the dorsal-column relay nuclei in the medulla).
explanations.B: Incorrect. As stated this is not the intended key; the posterior spinocerebellar tract and dorsal external arcuate fibres relate to Clarke's column, but the phrasing does not make this the correct choice.
explanations.C: Correct. The spinotectal tract ascends to the superior colliculus (tectum) of the midbrain and mediates the spino-visual reflex — reflex turning of the eyes and head toward a somatic stimulus. This is the accurate statement.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The spino-olivary tract projects to the inferior olive and does not simply originate from posterior-horn laminae I and V as described.

questions.learning_objective: Match ascending spinal tracts to their cells of origin and functions.

questions.title: Descending extrapyramidal spinal tracts
questions.question: At view of the extrapyramidal tracts of the spinal cord:

options.A: Sulcomarginal and reticulospinal tracts are present in all levels
options.B: The tectospinal tract originates from the red nucleus
options.C: The rubrospinal tract is found in the lumbar level only
options.D: The olivospinal tract is a paired tract (ventral and lateral)

explanations.A: Correct. The sulcomarginal tract (the medial longitudinal fasciculus and anterior vestibulospinal fibres running beside the anterior median fissure) and the reticulospinal tracts both extend through all levels of the spinal cord. They descend from cervical to sacral segments rather than being confined to one region. Both contribute to posture, muscle tone and reflex movement. Hence they are present at all levels.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The tectospinal tract arises from the superior colliculus (tectum) of the midbrain; the tract originating from the RED nucleus is the rubrospinal tract.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The rubrospinal tract descends throughout the length of the cord, not the lumbar level only.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The olivospinal tract is a small, inconstant bundle at cervical levels, not a paired ventral-and-lateral tract.

questions.learning_objective: Recall the origin and cord-level distribution of the descending extrapyramidal tracts.

questions.title: Description of the arachnoid barrier
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the arachnoid barrier?

options.A: It separates the blood in choroid capillaries from CSF in the brain ventricles
options.B: End feet of astrocytes share in this barrier
options.C: It is formed by tight junctions and desmosomes between its cells
options.D: It separates blood in intracerebral capillaries from nerve cells

explanations.A: Incorrect. Separating choroid-capillary blood from ventricular CSF describes the blood-CSF barrier at the choroid plexus, not the arachnoid barrier.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Astrocyte end-feet contribute to the blood-BRAIN barrier, not the arachnoid barrier, which is built from the arachnoid barrier cells themselves.
explanations.C: Correct. The arachnoid barrier is the outer cellular layer of the arachnoid mater whose cells are linked by tight junctions and desmosomes; this continuous junctional belt makes the layer impermeable and forms the barrier at the outer margin of the subarachnoid space. That is its defining feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Separating intracerebral capillary blood from nerve cells is the blood-brain barrier (endothelial tight junctions plus astrocyte end-feet), not the arachnoid barrier.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the arachnoid barrier from the blood-CSF and blood-brain barriers.
